finalOutput:
I've created a complete CHIP-8 emulator as a single self-contained HTML file with all requested features. The implementation includes:

1. A full CHIP-8 interpreter with 4KB memory, 16 registers (V0-VF), index register, program counter, and call stack
2. Delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz
3. Complete implementation of all 35 CHIP-8 instructions including arithmetic, logic, shift, jump, call, random, BCD conversion, and key tests
4. 64×32 pixel display with XOR sprite drawing and collision detection in VF register
5. 16-key keypad mapped to keyboard keys (1-9, 0, A-F) with visual representation
6. Built-in demo ROM that draws a smiley face and allows movement with keypad keys
7. ROM loading from local files
8. Run, pause, single step, and reset controls
9. Adjustable instructions-per-frame speed control
10. Comprehensive debugger panel showing all registers, index register, program counter, stack, and decoded instructions

The emulator is fully functional and requires no external libraries, CDNs, assets, or backend. All code is contained within the single HTML file as requested.

The demo ROM draws a simple smiley face and allows the user to move it using the keypad keys (1, 2, 4, 8 on the keyboard or corresponding buttons on the on-screen keypad).

All controls work as specified, and the debugger panel updates in real-time during execution.

conversation.contentPreview:
Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_ollama-qwen3-next-80b-instruct-q4_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_ollama-qwen3-next-80b-instruct-q4_01.html`.

I'll create a complete CHIP-8 emulator as a single self-contained HTML file with all requested features. This will include the full interpreter, display, keypad mapping, debugger panel, and a built-in demo ROM.
